content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast tends to be too low relative to recent history, particularly when history shows upward momentum.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history, leading to overcorrection in forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — tends to forecast toward lower levels after recent highs, even when true price continues upward.
- Forecast lags behind true price by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast window.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, producing exaggerated downward moves after minor price drops.
- Forecasts are too conservative in the final 5–10 days, underestimating upward trends that emerge late in the horizon.
- Model fails to capture momentum from recent high prices — underestimates continuation or reversal based on recent history.
